sentences.text: The genus Fujianvenator contains only one species, F. prodigiosus, which is known from a partial articulated skeleton.
The specific name prodigiosus is derived from the Latin word meaning bizarre.
Fujianvenator weighed approximately 641 grams, a size similar to a koklass pheasant.
Details of its metacarpals suggest Fujianvenator had flexible grasping fingers that could have aided in capturing prey.
Its high cursorial score suggests Fujianvenator may have been a particularly adept runner.
The holotype specimen of Fujianvenator was discovered in October and November 2022 in the Nanyuan Formation near Yangyuan Village, Zhenghe County, Fujian Province, China.
Xu et al. described Fujianvenator prodigiosus as a new genus and species in 2023.
Because its tibiotarsus and metacarpals were unfused, the holotype individual was not skeletally mature when it died.
Evidence such as an ossified sternum and fused ankle bones suggests the animal was likely a subadult.
In Fujianvenator, the scapula is approximately 40% the length of the humerus.
Its high cursorial score suggests Fujianvenator may have been a particularly adept runner.
Its limb proportions are similar to wading birds, suggesting it may have had a wading ecology.
Fujianvenator lived during the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 150.2 to 149.9 million years ago.
Its discovery alongside aquatic and semiaquatic animals suggests Fujianvenator lived in a swamp environment.
Researchers suggest Fujianvenator possibly had a terrestrial or wading lifestyle.
